summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 15, part 40), investigator Ray is confronted by Chief Becker about a murdered child aboard a starship. Becker dismisses the suspicion that the Lilaikens, a group of political terrorists, committed the crime, arguing the mutilation serves no purpose. Ray protests that the case is outside his assignment and that he lacks the training, but Becker says Captain Sorensen has already arranged for Ray to take the lead through CIU, pulling strings across deep space. The scene centers on Ray's frustration at being pulled off his mission and his career being jeopardized.
one_line: Investigator Ray is ordered by Chief Becker to lead a murder inquiry aboard a starship, despite his objections and mission duties.
key_facts: Becker argues the Lilaikens are political terrorists, not monsters, and that the child's body was mutilated in a way that gains them nothing.
Becker says the Lilaikens would have found a better way to dispose of the corpse if the kid had some kind of target value.
Ray says flatly that the investigation 'is not part of my assignment' and refuses to take it on.
Becker tells Ray that 'It's being made part of your assignment as of now.'
Ray states that he does not have the authority of the investigation's mission and that he has no time to do both.
Ray says he does not have the training for the job and that with New Holyoke two weeks out, the chances of suitable progress are close to nil.
Becker says the decision was made by Sorensen, the captain of the ship.
Becker states that Ray's superiors have already consented and that the captain called in a whole raft of favors to get Ray involved with CIU.
Becker tells Ray he has the freedom to poke around anonymously without freaking out the passengers.
Ray says he has all but confirmed the ship is clean of terrorists.
Ray notes that his career is being sucked down the cosmic drain as he is forced into the case.
Ray describes Becker as a man on the verge of strangling someone to satisfy his urge for vengeance.
